panel.reorderHelp: Drag to change the order, or hold Alt and use the up and down arrow keys. Alt and Home moves to the top. The five-hour window of the top tool is drawn on the tray icon.
panel.coach: The tray icon may be in the hidden icons area: open the arrow on the taskbar and drag the icon out. The panel now opens when you click the icon, not when you hover over it.
panel.empty.noneAdded: No tools on the main panel
panel.empty.noneDetail: A supported tool appears here once you install it.

quota.derived: These figures were decoded from the tool's own local data store. It is not a documented interface and may change silently when the tool updates.
quota.degraded: Data from this tool is not current; these figures are from the last readable measurement.
quota.lead: Quota is kept separately per model family.
quota.denial: These figures are this tool's own quota only. The model names below show the models you ran here; they have nothing to do with the quotas of tools that have their own row in the panel.
settings.back: Leave settings and return to the usage list
settings.metaTip.bridgeOn: A single line added to the {provider} settings (the bridge) passes the limit percentages to this app. It does not use the internet.
settings.metaTip.bridgeOff: The bridge is not in place, so the limit percentages are not updated. Tokens and cost still show. Press "Connect" to add it.
settings.metaTip.files: The records this tool writes on this computer are read directly; no connection is needed.
settings.metaTip.notFound: This tool was not found on this computer. It shows up on its own once installed.
settings.switchTip.on: The {provider} card is on the main panel. Click to remove it; no data is deleted.
settings.switchTip.off: The {provider} card is not on the main panel. Click to add it.
settings.models.help: Choose which tools appear on the main panel. Removing a tool only takes it off the list — it stays connected and no data is deleted.
settings.theme.title: Theme
settings.theme.help: With System, the Windows setting is followed.
settings.theme.helpSystem: Following the Windows dark/light setting — currently {resolved}. The panel changes when the setting does.
settings.language.help: The language of the panel, the tray icon and notices. With System, the Windows language is followed.
settings.autostart.label: Start with Windows
settings.autostart.help: LimitPeek starts in the tray when you sign in.
settings.autostart.byWindows: In the Microsoft Store version, Windows manages this: Settings → Apps → Startup.
settings.trayView.help: The strip shows usage in the taskbar, left of the clock; the tray icon hides meanwhile.
settings.trayView.unavailable: The taskbar strip cannot be shown on this computer; the tray icon is used instead.
settings.trayView.noRoom: There is no room on the taskbar for the strip: not even one tile fits between the icons and the clock. The tray icon is used instead.
app.trayViewNotSaved: The display setting could not be saved. The previous choice was restored.
settings.gauge.help: With rings, the outer ring is 5-hour usage and the inner ring weekly.
app.gaugeNotSaved: The gauge setting could not be saved. The previous choice was restored.
settings.glass.label: Transparency
settings.glass.help: The panel's background is see-through, like frosted glass; turn it off for a solid background. It turns off by itself when Windows high contrast is on.
settings.glass.bySystem: Transparency effects are off in Windows or high contrast is on, so the panel is not see-through now.
app.reduceTransparencyNotSaved: The transparency setting could not be saved. The previous choice was restored.
settings.disconnectConfirm.title: Disconnect {provider}?
settings.disconnectConfirm.detail: To read the limit percentages, LimitPeek added a single line to the {provider} settings; that line is the connection. Removing it takes a backup of the settings file first, and brings back your own status line if you had one. The percentages stop showing; tokens and cost keep showing.
settings.plan.hint: Automatic shows the plan the tool recorded for your account; you can pick one yourself.
settings.usage.intro: What each period's usage would have cost at published API prices. This is not a bill — you do not pay this amount (US dollars) under your subscription.
settings.usage.pending: Still counting {tools} usage; totals are incomplete.
settings.usage.empty: No local usage records were found yet.
settings.usage.noteNoDate: The price list's date was not reported.
settings.usage.incomplete: Some local records for {tools} could not be read; these periods may be undercounted.

coach.title: Show Claude Code's usage
coach.text: Adds a small status line bridge. It reads only the usage percentage and the reset time; it stores no chats, file paths or credentials.
coach.cancelled: Connection cancelled. No file was changed.
onboarding.welcome.title: Welcome to LimitPeek
onboarding.welcome.text: See the usage limits, token counts and API-price cost of Claude Code, Codex and your other AI coding tools in one place.
onboarding.welcome.privacyTitle: Your data stays on your computer
onboarding.welcome.privacy: The app only reads the records your tools write on this computer, and never connects to the internet on its own.
onboarding.tools.title: Tools found on this computer
onboarding.tools.text: Choose which ones to see in the panel. You can change this later in Settings → Tools.
onboarding.ready.title: You're all set
onboarding.ready.text: Open the panel from the LimitPeek icon on the taskbar. If you can't see the icon, open the ^ arrow at the right of the taskbar and drag the icon out.
